images.author: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases
images.why: Caption identifies a scanning electron micrograph of Ebola Makona virions, coloured red, on blue Vero cells. Strong contrasting colours; direct URL requests 3000-pixel width, although native dimensions were not verified.

images.author: NIAID Integrated Research Facility, Fort Detrick, Maryland
images.why: Caption identifies an SEM showing green Ebola particles budding from and attached to orange VERO E6 cells. Vivid filamentous morphology; direct URL requests 3000-pixel width, with native dimensions unverified.

images.author: CDC / Cynthia Goldsmith
images.why: Caption confirms a colourised TEM showing the filamentous, branching structure of an Ebola particle. This verified direct link is the lower-resolution preview; the page separately offers an 18.7 MB high-resolution download.

images.source: Purdue University, Department of Biological Sciences
images.author: Department of Biological Sciences, Purdue University
images.why: University image identifies EV71; the accompanying Purdue press-release caption describes a three-dimensional reconstruction of enterovirus 71. Conditional fallback only: no free-reuse licence confirmed, resolution unverified, and the linked image could not be retrieved by the browsing tool.

images.author: NIAID Integrated Research Facility, Fort Detrick, Maryland
images.why: Caption confirms a TEM showing blue West Nile virions replicating inside a red VERO E6 cell. Strong colour separation; direct URL requests 3000-pixel width, although native dimensions were not verified.

images.author: NIAID Integrated Research Facility, Fort Detrick, Maryland
